from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Area as a Function", [
            "Area function accumulates area over time.", 
            "Sliding boundary defines the interval.", 
            "Integration is a dynamic area process."
        ])
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 8, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda t: 2*t, x_range=[0, 4], color=WHITE)
        
        # Initial area under curve
        x_val = ValueTracker(2.0)
        
        def get_area():
            return axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_val.get_value()], color="#2ECC71", opacity=0.5)

        area = always_redraw(get_area)
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes, curve, area)
        
        # Boundary marker
        boundary_line = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_vertical_line(axes.input_to_graph_point(x_val.get_value(), curve), color="#9B59B6", stroke_width=4))
        self.add(boundary_line)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#9B59B6"))
        self.play(x_val.animate.set_value(3.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#ECF0F1"))
        self.play(x_val.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=2)
        self.play(x_val.animate.set_value(3.8), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Area rate equals current curve height.",
            "Adding a slice increases total area.",
            "Integration and differentiation are inverses.",
            "Derivative of area is original function.",
            "Area changes match the curve's height."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Connection: Differentiation and Integration", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2*x**2 + 0.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#E67E22")
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "D4")
        self.add(curve)
        dot = Dot(curve.point_from_proportion(0.6), color="#E67E22")
        self.add(dot)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3498DB")
        slice_rect = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[2, 2.3], dx=0.3, color="#3498DB")
        self.play(Create(slice_rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#F1C40F")
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["B5"], end=self.grid["D5"], color="#F1C40F")
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#E74C3C")
        derivative_text = MathTex(r"A'(x) = f(x)", color="#E74C3C")
        self.place_at_grid(derivative_text, "E2")
        self.play(Write(derivative_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#2ECC71")
        connection_line = Line(dot.get_center(), slice_rect.get_center(), color="#2ECC71")
        self.play(Create(connection_line))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC)", [
            "FTC links integral to antiderivative.",
            "Distance equals position change difference.",
            "Differentiation reveals local slopes.",
            "Integration recovers original accumulation.",
            "Inverse relationship completes the theorem."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Write FTC formula
        ftc_formula = MathTex(r"\int_{a}^{b} f(x) \, dx = F(b) - F(a)", color="#ECF0F1")
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(ftc_formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ECF0F1"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight fundamental theorem parts
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(ftc_formula, color="#E74C3C", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show inverse relationship with arrows
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['C4'], end=self.grid['D4'], color="#F1C40F")
        label = Text("f'(x) = f(x)", font_size=24, color="#F1C40F")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow), Write(label))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Animate application of FTC
        app_text = Text("Area = F(b) - F(a)", font_size=24, color="#2ECC71")
        self.place_at_grid(app_text, 'F2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(app_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final display of theorem in frame
        frame = Rectangle(width=4, height=2, color="#3498DB")
        self.place_in_area(frame, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(frame))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Summary", [
            "Derivatives find rate of change.",
            "Integrals track total accumulation.",
            "They are two linked perspectives."
        ])

        # Animation Setup
        clock_center = self.grid['C3']
        clock_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        clock_circle.move_to(clock_center)
        hand = Line(clock_center, clock_center + UP * 1.3, color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.play(Create(clock_circle), GrowFromCenter(hand))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        # Animate accumulation (angle swept)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        sector = always_redraw(lambda: Sector(
            arc_center=clock_center,
            radius=1.2,
            start_angle=PI/2,
            angle=-angle_tracker.get_value(),
            color="#E74C3C",
            fill_opacity=0.5
        ))
        hand.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(-angle_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.add(sector)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Accumulation Concept
sections.content: Use an animation of a 'Robot Vacuum' moving. Its speed (derivative) creates a path, and the area under the speed-time graph represents the total distance (integral) traveled. This visual establishes the link between 'rate of change' and 'accumulation'.
sections.example: A robot moves at 2m/s for 3 seconds. The area of the rectangle (2x3) equals the total distance (6m).

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Area as a Function
sections.content: Introduce the area function A(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t) dt. Visualize this as a 'sliding curtain' moving across a graph, covering more area as x increases. This prepares the student to see integration as a dynamic process.
sections.example: Visualize the region under f(t) = 2t being filled with liquid as the right boundary 'x' moves to the right.

sections.title: The Core Connection: Differentiation and Integration
sections.content: Present the derivative of the area function: d/dx [∫[a to x] f(t) dt] = f(x). Graphically show that adding a tiny slice of width Δx adds an area approximately equal to the height f(x) times the width. The rate at which area grows is exactly the height of the curve.
sections.example: If the area under a curve is 'A', then 'dA/dx' is the instantaneous height of the curve at x.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC)
sections.content: Formalize the theorem: ∫[a to b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a), where F' = f. Explain this as the 'inverse' relationship: differentiation strips away the area accumulation, while integration reconstructs the original function from its slope.
sections.example: Calculating the total distance (integral) by looking at the difference in position (antiderivative) at two specific time points.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Summarize the cycle: Derivative takes us from position to velocity (steepness), Integral takes us from velocity to position (accumulation). They are two sides of the same mathematical coin.
sections.example: Final animation: A clock hand spinning. Its velocity (derivative) defines its path, and the integral of its velocity over time returns the total angle swept (position).
